candidates.text:
Today is probably a good time to check in on things with @privy_io, which became part of @stripe just over a year ago.

Our acquisition was predicated on three factors: stablecoin growth, self-custody as a key enabler of broader global coverage, and rapidly increasing demand for programmable financial infrastructure. As we said at the time, "money has to reside somewhere, and Privy builds the world's best programmable vaults."

Since then, the Privy team has executed exceptionally well: assets in Privy wallets have grown ~25x, monthly active developers are up ~3x, revenue is up ~9x, and Privy now facilitates nearly $25B of monthly transaction volume. @tryramp, @Deel, @Klarna, @felixpago, @HyperliquidX, and thousands of other businesses are building embedded banking functionality on Privy.

At Stripe, we're deeply integrating Privy into Treasury, @Link, and Connect. In each case, it's accelerating our global expansion, and enabling us to build better functionality faster. (Coming soon: @Link balances.)

We're also seeing that Privy's wallet infrastructure is the ideal substrate for agents to transact and earn -- live today with @merit_systems, @orthogonal_sh, @Nevermined_ai, @prlnet, and more. Developers prefer programmable financial infrastructure, but agents need it. We expect that the agentic economy will continue to grow extremely quickly.

The Privy team has maintained remarkable product velocity, with major launches this year including deposit addresses, earning on Privy balances, digital asset accounts, custodial wallets, and Stripe's own stablecoin cards.

It's also been neat to see how Privy has been accelerated by Stripe, with better onramps, @stablecoin payment rails and licenses, Stripe's fiat capabilities and issuing stack, and integration with @Tempo.

Together, we're building one API for holding stablecoin balances and earning yield, moving money in and out of fiat, and orchestrating spend with cards. We still have a lot of work to do, not least in integrating everything across Privy, Bridge, and the rest of Stripe -- there's been so much feature and functionality expansion that we haven't yet had much time to reconcile everything. Overall, though, I'm very happy with how things are going, and excited by where these capabilities are headed.

If you're interested in working on the future of stablecoins, agentic payments, and crypto's deployment in the real world, you should get in touch with @sternhenri (now leading all of @StripeCrypto) or others on the team.

candidates.text:
Ramp is nearing 10% market share.  That is bad.  It sounds awesome..."Look at how much TPV we are doing $275 billion annualized TPV (cards and AP) in the $2.23 trillion corporate card market"

You don't want to build a company with "a lot of market share." You want to build a huge company. 

Once you cross "10% market share"...you can only grow ~10x from there!

Look at the other corporate card issuers.  Nielsen US Commercial Card Report (2024) implies Ramp, growing as fast as they are, could soon become the second biggest!
- AMEX has 24%
....Ramp?
- JPM has 10%
- BofA has 9%
- US Bank has 5%

Going from 0->10% is hard...but you can do it without upsetting anyone.  You can grow and everyone else can grow too. 

Going from 10-20% is even harder.  Growth becomes zero sum.  wonder why Mercury, Ramp and Airwallex are fighting on X...they are getting bigger and growth is increasingly zero sum!

Growing from 10->20% starts to reshape the entire industry

I said "this is bad".

The truth is "this is exciting".  

Ramp's mission is not "be the biggest corporate card company"....the mission is "save companies time and money."

Ramp has reached the end of the beginning of their story. 

Eric says as much "Chapter 1 is over.  Chapter 2 is just starting" (paraphrased).  

If you are investing in Ramp today, you are not investing in "the biggest corporate card company".  

You are investing in a company that has bigger mission.  

They need to keep growing market share, but more importantly, they need to grow their product lineup.  

JPM morgan is nearly a $1 trillion company.  Corporate cards are just a small small part of what they do. 

If Ramp wants to be a $1 trillion company...well...get back work.  

The whole Ramp team is well aware of the above.  Why do you think the focus on shipping new product so fast? why do you think they are launching AI products? 

Ramp is also in some ways a story of much of fintech at this point.  Robinhood is also at ~10% market share for example.  

The whole industry of plucky upstarts w/ <10% market share is now starting to change the entire ecosystem.  

I love this! I want the entire industry to change.  It is just starting.  Fintech is still early.

I look forward to seeing what Ramp (and everyone else) ships next!

I'm excited to watch them (and everyone else) continue to grow market share, but I'm even more excited to see what their products might become.  What if corporate cards turn out to be just a small part of what Ramp does in the future? 

If that happens, I'm here for it!

*re: market share.  Ramps TPV includes all forms of spend, not just card spend.  so it's hard to get an exact market share percentage.  "is nearing 10%" is not precise, but directionally correct.  Also if you're growing 100% a year, the broad points made in this post still apply (or will apply very soon!).

The biggest lesson I've learnt from Eric and Karim is conviction.

Writing is the opposite of guessing the sweets in the jar, where the average is powerful.

In writing, the average is useless. Not because people’s opinions are useless, but because the sum of them is. All everyone can agree on is “we’re a better way”.

Good writing is aggressive. You are saying, “Listen to me, I have something to tell you” — and only an individual can write like that.

Earlier this year, I was struggling to write Ramp’s careers page. I was trying to write something everyone liked. Karim didn't care about that. He wrote, “We only hire builders”. I made it the headline and it got one million views.
